newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Oil erases gains on ample prompt supply.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Oil erases gains on ample prompt supply.

text.p: Oil markets gave up early gains to end weaker on Wednesday as traders focused on prompt oversupply of crude oil.
European crude markets are awash with crude and only a pick-up in gasoline demand from the United States is likely to rescue world prices, they said.
"When refineries start coming back on stream prices will probably drift lower unless there is gasoline demand from the States," said Scott Carter, senior oil trader at Tosco Petroleum in London.

Several important oil refineries in Europe and Asia have been shut for scheduled maintenance in recent weeks, lending support to certain oil product markets but depressing demand for their main feedstock, crude oil.
London May futures for North Sea bellwether Brent Blend crude closed 26 cents lower at $19.28 a barrel.
Prices for Brent have fallen from just under $25 a barrel to what many dealers see as a temporary low of less than $19 at the start of this month.
Soggy market conditions ahead of the Easter holiday left trading generally thin on Wednesday with few fresh headlines to buffet prices.
The Russian oil industry was relaxed about a planned strike on Thursday by up to 20 million people in Russia.

"Practically nobody from Novorossiisk will take part in the protests tomorrow and there certainly won't be any actions to affect operations," said Valentin Korzh, chief engineer at Novorossiisk, Russia's main outlet for oil to the West.
The market was also unmoved by the continued loss of 100,000 barrels per day of Nigerian crude oil production in a political feud there.

Anglo-Dutch operator Royal Dutch/Shell said its exports would be unaffected by the unrest in Nigeria, where three people have been killed in protest riots in which some 100 Shell oil workers have been held hostage.
Nigeria, with output of about 2.15 million bpd, is the fifth largest producer in the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC).
